options.summary: Run more same-task Causality paired online smokes before changing the logging protocol.
Broaden cross-task failure-mode coverage with additional no-valid or evaluator-stress trajectories.
Prioritize complete prospective attention/taste gate logging before stronger human-efficiency or taste-effect claims.

rationale: The package already contains executable traces, repeated smoke evidence, and a clean-clone audit, but the top-conference readiness audit still blocks human-efficiency and taste-effect claims because archived real gates lack complete attention-cost records and most lack structured taste/insight fields. The scientifically stronger next move is to make the human gate observable before adding more weak performance runs.

downstream_budget.next_evidence_milestone: complete prospective attention+taste logging on future live gates before attention-efficiency or taste-effect claims
downstream_budget.interpretation: operator-recorded measurement-readiness gate, not a performance result

attention_cost.notes: Operator-recorded gate from the live Codex paper-development thread. Use as measurement-readiness evidence only; do not treat as independent human-subject timing or downstream performance evidence.

taste_insight.qualitative_rationale: This decision favors an evidence structure that can reveal whether human scientific taste acts as a high-variance search prior, even if it delays additional benchmark wins. It is valuable because it makes the paper’s distinctive human-in-the-loop claim auditable rather than decorative.

follow_up_checks: Rerun attention-cost and taste/insight audits after writing this gate.
Update the manuscript to distinguish measurement-readiness evidence from performance evidence.
